page.h1: HTS Chapter 88: Aircraft, Spacecraft, and Parts Thereof — Foreign Tariff Changes on U.S. Exports

seo.title: Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Aircraft Exports Since 2025 (HTS Ch. 88) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What China, the EU, Canada and other buyers changed on U.S. aircraft, spacecraft and parts since January 2025, and what is coming.

intro: The only measure that costs U.S. aircraft and spacecraft exporters money today is **China's extra 10%** on all U.S. goods, which reaches finished aircraft and most parts — and could rise back toward the 34% it started at if the rest of the suspension lapses on **January 10, 2027**. The bigger story for this chapter is the one to watch rather than pay: the **EU extended, on July 6, 2026, its suspension of the retaliatory tariffs from the 17-year Boeing/Airbus dispute**, so none of the EU's WTO-authorized countermeasures on U.S. aircraft are in force. Canada, Mexico, the UK, Japan, Switzerland and Brazil have not added any tariff on U.S. aircraft or parts since January 2025.
scope: The 9 largest markets for U.S. Chapter 88 goods (73% of 2025 exports).

upcoming.title: China's suspension of 24 points of its extra tariff on U.S. goods ends
upcoming.whatHappens: China suspended 24 points of its extra tariff on all U.S. goods for one year from November 10, 2025, keeping 10%. In September 2026 the two sides agreed to extend the arrangement to January 10, 2027, with talks on a further extension expected before the end of the year.
upcoming.impact: If the suspension lapses without a further extension, China's extra tariff on U.S. goods — including Chapter 88 aircraft and parts — would rise from 10% back toward the 34% level it fell to after the April 2025 peak. Talks on a further extension were reported before the end of 2026, so a lapse is not the base case, but no replacement notice has been published yet.
upcoming.status: Extension to Jan 10, 2027 announced by MOFCOM; China's Tariff Commission has not yet published its notice

inEffect.measure: Extra tariff on all U.S. goods cut to 10%
inEffect.appliesTo: All Chapter 88 goods of U.S. origin, including finished aircraft (8802), on top of China's normal rate — low on large aircraft (about 1% on the 8802.40 line found for this report) and zero on many imported aviation-maintenance parts (engines, landing gear, consumables) under China's own duty exemption for materials domestic industry cannot supply (Cai Guan Shui [2021] No. 15, in force 2021–2030). Reports from April–May 2025 said China would also exempt engines, nacelles and landing gear from the new tariff on U.S. goods specifically, but China has not published an English-language notice confirming that exact carve-out, and one legal analysis of the April 2025 announcement said the increased tariff portion would not be eligible for ordinary exemption and reduction policies — so treat relief for those parts as reported, not confirmed. Finished aircraft are not exempted either way.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $20M shipment of U.S.-made aircraft parts pays an extra $2M under the 10% tariff, on top of whatever ordinary duty applies to that line — zero for parts that qualify for China's maintenance-materials exemption, roughly 1% for most other lines. The extra rate peaked at 125% in April 2025; 24 of those points are suspended, now until January 10, 2027 — see What's coming.

changes.title: U.S.–China Board of Trade product lists
changes.status: Recommended for reduced tariffs; no Chinese tariff cut published yet
changes.detail: China's import list under the U.S.–China Board of Trade “30-for-30” framework names 1,619 Chinese tariff lines that could get lower tariffs on U.S. goods. No Chinese tariff cut has been published yet.

changes.title: Counter-tariffs on U.S. products (answering U.S. Section 338 tariffs)
changes.detail: Counter-tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on listed U.S. products, mostly steel, aluminum, dairy, appliances, furniture and clothing.

changes.title: Brazil has imposed nothing on U.S. goods; it is challenging U.S. tariffs at the WTO
changes.status: Nothing imposed on U.S. goods; talks ongoing
changes.detail: Brazil has published no countermeasure on U.S. goods. Its Economic Reciprocity Law (Law 15,122 of April 11, 2025) would allow them — such as import restrictions or suspending intellectual-property obligations — but none has been applied. On July 27, 2026 Brazil asked the United States for WTO consultations over U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, and Brazilian ministers met USTR on August 31 and September 30, 2026 to set up a working group on a possible agreement.

changes.title: EU extends suspension of its Boeing/Airbus-dispute retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods
changes.status: Suspended since July 11, 2021; extended by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1549 from July 11, 2026
changes.detail: The U.S. and EU suspended, for five years from July 11, 2021, the tariffs each had imposed or threatened in their 17-year WTO dispute over Boeing and Airbus subsidies (the EU's WTO-authorized countermeasures covered up to $4 billion of U.S. goods, large civil aircraft among them, under the Cooperative Framework for Large Civil Aircraft). Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1549 of July 6, 2026 extends the EU's suspension past its July 10, 2026 expiry; the U.S. has not reactivated its Section 301 tariffs from the same dispute either.

changes.title: USMCA stays in force: Canada and Mexico keep 0% on qualifying U.S. goods
changes.detail: At the first USMCA joint review on July 1, 2026 the three countries did not agree to a new 16-year term, so the agreement is now reviewed every year; it stays in force until at least July 1, 2036. Canada and Mexico keep applying USMCA rates to qualifying U.S. goods.

changes.title: EU–U.S. framework tariff cuts adopted
changes.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 cuts EU duties on listed U.S. goods to zero from July 1, 2026, and Regulation (EU) 2026/1461 sets aside duties on certain other goods.

changes.title: Mexico raises its general tariffs on goods from countries without a trade agreement
changes.status: In force since Jan 1, 2026; U.S. goods still enter under USMCA
changes.detail: The decree raises Mexico's general (MFN) rates on more than 1,400 tariff lines, mostly cars, textiles, clothing, steel, plastics and footwear. U.S. goods that qualify for USMCA keep their preferential rate. Mexico has published no counter-tariff on U.S. goods.

changes.title: Reciprocity petition against the 2025 U.S. tariffs: framing approved, action deferred
changes.detail: Camex's executive committee (Gecex) approved the Foreign Ministry's petition as falling under the Economic Reciprocity Law and chose to await diplomatic consultations before forming the working group that would propose countermeasures. Nothing was imposed.

changes.title: U.S.–UK pharmaceutical pricing arrangement
changes.status: In force; full text agreed Apr 2, 2026
changes.detail: Not a tariff: the UK raises the net price it pays for new medicines by about 25% and lifts NICE’s cost-effectiveness threshold. UK tariffs on medicines stay at zero.

changes.title: U.S.–Switzerland–Liechtenstein trade framework
changes.detail: Switzerland intends to apply zero duties on all U.S. industrial goods.

changes.title: China extends its tariff exclusions for U.S. goods to December 31, 2026
changes.detail: Under the November 2025 U.S.–China deal, China extended its market-based exclusion process for imports from the United States; exclusions stay valid until December 31, 2026. They lift China's 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods (answering the U.S. Section 301 tariffs), which were never repealed.

changes.title: U.S.–Japan agreement
changes.detail: Executive Order 14345 implements the U.S.–Japan agreement: Japan works toward buying U.S. farm and other goods worth $8 billion a year and investing in the U.S.

changes.title: EU countermeasures on about €93B of U.S. goods
changes.detail: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1564 listed about €93B of U.S. goods for extra duties from September 7, 2025. The measures were suspended from August 6, 2025, again from February 7, 2026, and from August 7, 2026 with no end date (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1893).

changes.title: Extra tariff on all U.S. goods cut to 10%
changes.status: In force; 24-point suspension extended to Jan 10, 2027
changes.detail: Rose 34% → 84% → 125% in April 2025 (125% from April 12), then cut to 10% from May 14, 2025 with 24 points suspended for 90 days. The suspension was extended for 90 days from August 12, 2025 and for one year from November 10, 2025, with the 10% kept. In September 2026 the two sides agreed to extend the arrangement to January 10, 2027. Applies to every U.S.-origin good on top of China’s normal rate.

changes.title: U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal
changes.detail: UK concessions were a beef quota and a duty-free ethanol quota.

changes.title: 25% counter-tariff on C$30B of U.S. goods
changes.detail: 25% counter-tariff on C$30B of U.S. goods. Canada repealed most of it on Sept 1, 2025, keeping only the steel, aluminum and auto surtaxes.
